name: param-space-codim2-structure
title: Codim-2 Bistability Wedge (Beer 2022)
question:
How is the single-neuron 1→3 transition organised (saddle-node fold curves and a cusp) when both the self-weight
and the bias vary — what is the shape of the bistable region in the
(self-weight, bias) plane?
hypothesis:
Two saddle-node fold curves meet at a cusp and bound a connected wedge of
bistability (three equilibria) that opens as self-weight increases; the
center-crossing pitchfork is the cusp's symmetric axis — the codimension-2 organising structure of
Beer (2022).
objective:
Compute the equilibrium count over a 2-D grid of (self-weight, bias) for a
single neuron and render the parameter-plane map, identifying the bistable
wedge.
claim:
Bistability occupies a connected cusp wedge in (self-weight, bias), reproducing
the codim-2 structure of Beer (2022).
description:
`param_space.codim2_equilibria_count` evaluates the equilibrium count over the
(w, θ) grid; the gallery renders it as a heatmap. A bistable (3-equilibria)
region is present and connected, bounded by two saddle-node fold curves meeting at a cusp (the center-crossing
pitchfork is its symmetric axis); cells exactly on the
fold can register 2 equilibria.

expected_behavior.name: bistable-wedge-present
expected_behavior.condition: single neuron, grid over self-weight × bias
expected_behavior.rationale:
The maximum equilibrium count over the grid is 3, and the 3-equilibria cells
form a connected wedge opening toward high self-weight — the cusp.

findings.summary: Connected bistable wedge found; max equilibrium count = 3 over the grid.
findings.detail:
The codim-2 map (figures/codim2.png) shows a yellow (3-equilibria) wedge
opening at high self-weight and bounded by two fold curves meeting at a cusp, with a boundary
cell at exactly 2 equilibria sitting on the fold.

derived.insight: Connected bistable wedge found; max equilibrium count = 3 over the grid.
